name: Advance Fee Loan Scams
summary: A guaranteed loan, no credit check, requires an upfront fee that you pay and a loan that never arrives.

typicalLoss.note: Charged in escalating instalments to people who are already in financial distress.

howItWorks.detail: Lamp poles, WhatsApp broadcasts, Facebook groups and SMS blasts. 'Blacklisted welcome. No credit check. Same day payout.'
You are approved within minutes for an amount you did not really justify. Legitimate credit providers are legally required to assess affordability.
An initiation fee, an insurance premium, a legal or administration charge, payable before the loan is released. Legitimate fees are deducted from the loan, never paid in advance.
Once the first fee is paid, a second is required: a compliance charge, a clearance fee, a bank verification deposit. Sunk cost keeps people paying.
The application collects your ID, payslip, bank statements and sometimes banking login details, a full identity package for later fraud.

redFlags: Any fee payable before a loan is disbursed.
'Blacklisted welcome' or 'no credit check' promises. Registered credit providers must run affordability checks by law.
The lender is not registered with the National Credit Regulator, or quotes an NCR number that does not check out.
Contact only through WhatsApp or a cellphone number, with no physical office.
You are asked for your online banking username and password 'to verify income'.
illustrativeCase: A retail worker declined by two banks answers a WhatsApp advert offering R30 000 with no credit check. She is approved in eleven minutes and asked for a R1 200 'credit life insurance premium'. She pays. A R2 400 'NCR compliance clearance' follows, then a R3 000 'bank verification deposit'. She borrows to pay each one. The number goes dead at R6 600.
howToProtect: Verify every lender on the NCR register before any contact. It is free and takes a minute.
Hold the line: legitimate lenders deduct fees from the loan amount and never require a payment first.
Understand that 'blacklisted welcome' is not a service offering, it is a filter for finding vulnerable people.
Never share online banking credentials with a lender. No legitimate one asks.
If you are in genuine debt distress, speak to a registered debt counsellor rather than a same-day lender.
ifYouveBeenHit: Stop paying. There is no final fee, and the loan does not exist.
Report to the National Credit Regulator and the SAPS.
If you gave banking credentials, change them immediately and alert your bank.
Register a SAFPS protective listing if you handed over ID and payslip documents.
Check your credit report for accounts opened using your details.

faqs.q: Are initiation fees not legal in South Africa?
faqs.a: They are, but the National Credit Act allows them to be deducted from or added to the loan, not collected in cash before disbursement.

faqs.q: They gave me an NCR number, so are they registered?
faqs.a: Check it yourself on the NCR register. Quoted numbers are frequently copied from real credit providers.

faqs.q: Can I get the fees back?
faqs.a: Rarely. Report anyway, because volume of complaints is what drives enforcement against these operations.
